Laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) enables trace microalloying to form hierarchical (TiB + Y2O3) nanodispersions in near-α TA15 alloy: a quasi-continuous TiB network along primary-β grain boundaries plus intragranular Y2O3 nanoparticles. Despite totalling only 0.35 vol% reinforcements, this LPBF-architected structure achieves >10% strength gain at room temperature and, notably, 15% gain at 500°C while retaining comparable ductility — surpassing conventional composites that need an order-of-magnitude more reinforcements. This enhanced performance originates from synergistic strengthening mechanisms enabled by the thermally stable hierarchical nanodispersions. Therefore, precursor-assisted LPBF microalloying provides a useful strategy for designing high-strength near-α titanium alloys with minimal nominal reinforcement addition after process-window optimisation. https://github.com/lwz20210407/ZotWatch/issues/new?title=%5BZotWatch+feedback%5D+%E6%9A%82%E7%BC%93%E8%87%AA%E5%8A%A8%E6%8E%A8%E8%8D%90+Automatic-Differentiation-Enabled+Finite+Element+Model+Updating%3A+Learning+constitutive+neu&body=%3C%21--+zotwatch-feedback-v2+--%3E%0A%60%60%60json%0A%7B%22doi%22%3A+%2210.1016%2Fj.cma.2026.119492%22%2C+%22rating%22%3A+%22later%22%2C+%22facets%22%3A+%5B%22calibration%22%5D%2C+%22reason%22%3A+%22%22%2C+%22applicability%22%3A+%22hold%22%7D%0A%60%60%60%0A%E5%85%AC%E5%BC%80%E5%8F%8D%E9%A6%88%EF%BC%8C%E8%AF%B7%E5%8B%BF%E5%A1%AB%E5%86%99%E7%A7%81%E4%BA%BA%E7%AC%94%E8%AE%B0%E3%80%82 The identification of constitutive neural network models from heterogeneous full-field deformation data provides a robust alternative to traditional calibration methods based on homogeneous stress–strain experiments, particularly given the high dimensionality of trainable parameters. Existing approaches must balance generality, robustness, and computational efficiency: Conventional finite element model updating is broadly applicable but computationally demanding; weak-form methods offer efficiency but are sensitive to noise and data scarcity; neural operator models are highly expressive but require extensive training datasets. This work presents ADE-FEMU (Automatic-Differentiation-Enabled Finite Element Model Updating), an end-to-end differentiable framework that integrates a constitutive neural network model within a JAX-FEM nonlinear solver and identifies its parameters through gradient-based minimization of a measurement-mismatch loss, allowing for training on structural data with limited kinetic information. Thus, it can be considered as an extension of finite element model updating (FEMU) for hyperelastic materials, implemented within a GPU-accelerated, fully automatically differentiable finite element framework Newton tangent stiffness and loss gradients are computed automatically using forward- and reverse-mode automatic differentiation throughout the entire pipeline, thereby removing the need for analytic adjoints or offline surrogate models. ADE-FEMU is demonstrated for two architectures: a grey-box Constitutive Artificial Neural Network (CANN), a polyconvex, fully connected model with high flexibility, and a white-box CANN, an expert-system network with phenomenologically interpretable strain–energy terms. Focusing on incompressible isotropic hyperelasticity, ADE-FEMU is evaluated on three open experimental datasets: (1) full digital image correlation (DIC) of a perforated tensile specimen, (2) a reduced-data scenario with a one-dimensional stretch profile and global force–displacement curve, and (3) a heterogeneous matrix–inclusion system in which both phases’ constitutive laws are identified and generalized to twenty-two previously unseen samples. The grey-box CANN demonstrates superior performance with comprehensive, full-field, or heterogeneous data, whereas the interpretable white-box CANN is more reliable for model discovery from sparse datasets. The source code will be released upon publication. Published: 2026-10-24T00:00:00+00:00 Venue: Computer Methods in Applied Mechanics and Engineering 研究类型: 跨金属方法参考

公开阅读反馈 暂缓自动推荐: https://github.com/lwz20210407/ZotWatch/issues/new?title=%5BZotWatch+feedback%5D+%E6%9A%82%E7%BC%93%E8%87%AA%E5%8A%A8%E6%8E%A8%E8%8D%90+Deformation-induced+damage+in+finitely-strained+metal+sheets%3A+Large-area+damage+quantifica&body=%3C%21--+zotwatch-feedback-v2+--%3E%0A%60%60%60json%0A%7B%22doi%22%3A+%2210.1016%2Fj.ijsolstr.2026.114393%22%2C+%22rating%22%3A+%22later%22%2C+%22facets%22%3A+%5B%22ductile_fracture%22%2C+%22damage_evolution%22%2C+%22other_metals%22%5D%2C+%22reason%22%3A+%22%22%2C+%22applicability%22%3A+%22hold%22%7D%0A%60%60%60%0A%E5%85%AC%E5%BC%80%E5%8F%8D%E9%A6%88%EF%BC%8C%E8%AF%B7%E5%8B%BF%E5%A1%AB%E5%86%99%E7%A7%81%E4%BA%BA%E7%AC%94%E8%AE%B0%E3%80%82 Reliable identification of damage-induced property changes in formed metal sheets remains challenging because plastic deformation alters the mechanical response through several coupled mechanisms. Moreover, pronounced ductile damage evolution occurs predominantly under inhomogeneous states of deformation, e.g., strain localization, which compromises the characterization of potential effects of damage on macroscopic mechanical properties, e.g., elastic stiffness. In this study, damage in dual-phase steel DP800 sheets is isolated from other concurrent mechanisms using a novel “sheet extrusion” process. The flat, finitely-strained sheets exhibit large regions with homogeneous properties, enabling subsequent characterization of damage-induced property changes. Damage in the form of microscopic voids is then characterized by large-area scanning electron microscopy (SEM) measurements, and damage-induced property changes are determined by subsequent characterization tests on specimens extracted from the extruded sheets. It is found that deformation-induced damage does not measurably affect the apparent elastic stiffness or the pre-necking tensile response. In contrast, differences in fracture-related performance quantities, i.e., the remaining ductility and the tensile impact energy, indicate that higher deformation-induced damage promotes earlier macroscopic failure by increasing the likelihood of local void coalescence during subsequent loading. https://github.com/lwz20210407/ZotWatch/issues/new?title=%5BZotWatch+feedback%5D+%E6%9A%82%E7%BC%93%E8%87%AA%E5%8A%A8%E6%8E%A8%E8%8D%90+Stress-state+redistribution+and+thickness-ratio+dependence+of+ballistic+resistance+in+duct&body=%3C%21--+zotwatch-feedback-v2+--%3E%0A%60%60%60json%0A%7B%22doi%22%3A+%2210.1063%2F5.0356353%22%2C+%22rating%22%3A+%22later%22%2C+%22facets%22%3A+%5B%22stress_state%22%2C+%22impact_validation%22%2C+%22other_metals%22%5D%2C+%22reason%22%3A+%22%22%2C+%22applicability%22%3A+%22hold%22%7D%0A%60%60%60%0A%E5%85%AC%E5%BC%80%E5%8F%8D%E9%A6%88%EF%BC%8C%E8%AF%B7%E5%8B%BF%E5%A1%AB%E5%86%99%E7%A7%81%E4%BA%BA%E7%AC%94%E8%AE%B0%E3%80%82 Thin high-strength 7075-T651 aluminum plates are susceptible to radial cracking, petaling, and rear-face fragmentation under ogive-nosed projectile impact. This study investigates the influence of a ductile 2024-T351 front layer on the ballistic response and failure evolution of a thin 7075-T651 substrate. Ballistic experiments were conducted on 1.59-mm monolithic 7075-T651 targets and 2.4/1.59-mm 2024-T351/7075-T651 bilayer targets, and the results were combined with three-dimensional finite-element simulations employing material-specific constitutive and fracture models. The bilayer configuration exhibited an experimental ballistic-limit velocity of 184.8 m/s, compared with 102.4 m/s for the monolithic 7075-T651 target, corresponding to a configuration-level increase of 80.5%. At comparable normalized impact velocities, the selected failed elements in the 7075-T651 rear plate of the bilayer target exhibited a distribution shifted toward higher positive damage-averaged stress triaxiality compared with those in the monolithic target. This shift was accompanied by a more localized damaged region and petaling in the bilayer rear plate, linking the presence of the 2024-T351 front layer to changes in both stress-state histories and failure morphology. Buckingham π analysis and seven parametric simulations further established a dimensionally consistent semi-empirical relation between ballistic-limit velocity and front-to-rear thickness ratio, Vbl=153.7trR2=0.997, while the incremental ballistic benefit decreased with increasing tr. These results link ductile-front-induced stress-state redistribution with failure-mode evolution and provide a quantitative framework for thickness allocation in layered aluminum targets. https://github.com/lwz20210407/ZotWatch/issues/new?title=%5BZotWatch+feedback%5D+%E6%9A%82%E7%BC%93%E8%87%AA%E5%8A%A8%E6%8E%A8%E8%8D%90+A+knowledge-distilled+artificial+neural+network+constitutive+model+for+finite+element+simu&body=%3C%21--+zotwatch-feedback-v2+--%3E%0A%60%60%60json%0A%7B%22doi%22%3A+%2210.20517%2Fjmi.2026.52%22%2C+%22rating%22%3A+%22later%22%2C+%22facets%22%3A+%5B%22temperature%22%2C+%22strain_rate%22%2C+%22plasticity_hardening%22%2C+%22umat_implementation%22%5D%2C+%22reason%22%3A+%22%22%2C+%22applicability%22%3A+%22hold%22%7D%0A%60%60%60%0A%E5%85%AC%E5%BC%80%E5%8F%8D%E9%A6%88%EF%BC%8C%E8%AF%B7%E5%8B%BF%E5%A1%AB%E5%86%99%E7%A7%81%E4%BA%BA%E7%AC%94%E8%AE%B0%E3%80%82 Accurate, computationally deployable constitutive models are required for reliable finite element (FE) simulations of metallic hot deformation. This study develops a knowledge-distilled artificial neural network (KD-ANN) constitutive model for β-C titanium alloy using 24 flow-stress curves measured at 800-1,050 °C and strain rates of 0.01-10 s -1 . An Extra Trees model serves as the teacher, while a compact multilayer perceptron provides a continuous constitutive mapping with explicit derivative evaluation for FE implementation. The student is trained using experimental and teacher supervision, weighted Huber loss, curve-balanced weighting and enhanced weighting in the low-strain region. Following preliminary teacher-algorithm and student-configuration screening, temperature-wise predictive performance is evaluated using curve-grouped leave-one-temperature-out validation. In each fold, all four curves at the target temperature are held out, while the fold-specific KD-ANN and modified Johnson–Cook (J–C) models are fitted using only the retained temperature conditions. Across the six held-out-temperature folds, KD-ANN achieves mean values of the coefficient of determination = 0.984, root mean square error = 11.40 MPa and mean absolute error (MAE) = 9.21 MPa, compared with 0.960, 17.12 and 12.58 MPa, respectively, for the modified J–C model. Sequential ablation and targeted control experiments show that the joint use of experimental stresses and teacher-generated targets produces the largest incremental improvement within the tested training framework. The trained student network is implemented in Abaqus through a VUHARD user subroutine. For the fold in which the lower-boundary temperature of 800 °C is held out from model fitting and validation, the FE load–displacement predictions yield a mean MAE of 0.729 kN, compared with 1.213 kN for the modified J–C model. These results demonstrate improved prediction of complete flow curves at unseen temperatures within the investigated range and support the use of KD-ANN as a constitutive input for hot-compression simulations. This study quantifies the mechanical degradation caused by locally introduced rubber-glove contamination in stress-relieved PBF-LB/M Ti-6Al-4V. Rubber-glove fragments were inserted into defined build layers of standardized tensile specimens and into highly loaded transition regions of a topology-optimized bracket demonstrator. Twelve uncontaminated and twelve contaminated tensile specimens and nine brackets per condition were evaluated. The contaminated tensile specimens exhibited a mean ultimate strength of approx. 860 MPa compared with approx. 1200 MPa for the reference condition, corresponding to a reduction of approx. 28%. Mean elongation at break decreased from approx. 13.4% to 0.6%, representing a reduction of approx. 95%. Fracture preferentially occurred at the contamination insertion region and was associated with planar fracture features and retained spherical powder particles. The results support a predominantly defect-controlled degradation mechanism associated with locally disturbed consolidation. Published: 2026-10-28T00:00:00+00:00 Venue: Alloys 研究类型: TC4核心研究

https://github.com/lwz20210407/ZotWatch/issues/new?title=%5BZotWatch+feedback%5D+%E6%9A%82%E7%BC%93%E8%87%AA%E5%8A%A8%E6%8E%A8%E8%8D%90+Finite+Deformation+Analysis+for+Fatigue+and+Creep%E2%80%90Fatigue+Evaluation+Under+Cyclic+Thermo%E2%80%90M&body=%3C%21--+zotwatch-feedback-v2+--%3E%0A%60%60%60json%0A%7B%22doi%22%3A+%2210.1111%2Fffe.70482%22%2C+%22rating%22%3A+%22later%22%2C+%22facets%22%3A+%5B%22umat_implementation%22%5D%2C+%22reason%22%3A+%22%22%2C+%22applicability%22%3A+%22hold%22%7D%0A%60%60%60%0A%E5%85%AC%E5%BC%80%E5%8F%8D%E9%A6%88%EF%BC%8C%E8%AF%B7%E5%8B%BF%E5%A1%AB%E5%86%99%E7%A7%81%E4%BA%BA%E7%AC%94%E8%AE%B0%E3%80%82 ABSTRACT This study develops a cyclic thermo‐elasto‐plastic creep constitutive model within a finite‐deformation framework for structures under cyclic thermo‐mechanical loading. The A‐K‐O kinematic hardening model is combined with a Norton‐Bailey creep law, and the governing equations are discretized using a backward‐Euler return‐mapping algorithm. A consistent tangent stiffness matrix is derived to improve the convergence of nonlinear finite element analyses. Plastic dissipation is further introduced as an internal heat source in a sequentially coupled thermo‐mechanical formulation. Numerical examples show that the finite‐deformation formulation captures large plastic deformation more accurately than the small‐deformation assumption, that creep during load holding promotes ratcheting and stress redistribution, and that plastic dissipation under rapid cyclic loading produces substantial temperature rise. The proposed framework provides a stable numerical basis for evaluating deformation and heat generation in components under cyclic thermo‐mechanical loading. item.title: A coupled crystal plasticity-damage RVE framework for predicting macroscopic ductile fracture locus
item.description: 库内相似论文：Modeling of ductile fracture from shear to balanced biaxial tension for sheet metals（相似度 0.762） 引用重点论文：Application of extended Mohr–Coulomb criterion to ductile fracture [https://doi.org/10.1007/s10704-009-9422-8] 复杂应力状态与屈服准则: 可作为屈服面形式、压力/Lode 依赖与试样构型设计的比较线索（规则推断，非已验证迁移） 迁移前检查: 核对应力状态覆盖范围、是否含负三轴度、加载路径是否比例 摘要片段: The damage parameters are calibrated using … 标题/摘要不能确认全部实验条件与方法适用性，未陈述内容保持未知 延性断裂准则: 可作为断裂轨迹形式与起裂判据的比较线索（规则推断，非已验证迁移） 迁移前检查: 核对标定试样组合、是否覆盖你的应力状态区间、有无独立验证试样 摘要片段: Predicting the macroscopic ductile fracture locus … 标题/摘要不能确认全部实验条件与方法适用性，未陈述内容保持未知 摘要方法线索: crystal plasticity 局限/不适用线索；摘要句子层面的规则线索，不等同于对某篇被引论文的评价 摘要方法线索: Mohr-Coulomb 改进扩展线索；采用方法线索；摘要句子层面的规则线索，不等同于对某篇被引论文的评价 公开阅读反馈 直接有用: https://github.com/lwz20210407/ZotWatch/issues/new?title=%5BZotWatch+feedback%5D+%E6%9A%82%E7%BC%93%E8%87%AA%E5%8A%A8%E6%8E%A8%E8%8D%90+A+coupled+crystal+plasticity-damage+RVE+framework+for+predicting+macroscopic+ductile+fract&body=%3C%21--+zotwatch-feedback-v2+--%3E%0A%60%60%60json%0A%7B%22doi%22%3A+%2210.1016%2Fj.matdes.2026.117330%22%2C+%22rating%22%3A+%22later%22%2C+%22facets%22%3A+%5B%22stress_state%22%2C+%22ductile_fracture%22%5D%2C+%22reason%22%3A+%22%22%2C+%22applicability%22%3A+%22hold%22%7D%0A%60%60%60%0A%E5%85%AC%E5%BC%80%E5%8F%8D%E9%A6%88%EF%BC%8C%E8%AF%B7%E5%8B%BF%E5%A1%AB%E5%86%99%E7%A7%81%E4%BA%BA%E7%AC%94%E8%AE%B0%E3%80%82 Predicting the macroscopic ductile fracture locus of sheet metals directly from microstructural simulations remains challenging. This work develops a coupled crystal plasticity–damage framework that links a slip-system-level continuum damage model with a representative volume element (RVE) failure criterion, enabling direct construction of the macroscopic fracture locus from virtual experiments on AA6061-T6 alloy. Implemented in the DAMASK spectral solver, the damage model introduces four parameters governing damage rate, stress-state sensitivity, slip-history nonlinearity, and the incubation threshold. A multi-grain void-cluster connectivity criterion is proposed to define RVE failure without relying on numerical termination. The damage parameters are calibrated using uniaxial and plane-strain tension fracture strains from the modified Mohr–Coulomb (MMC3) locus and then tested under four proportional stress states from simple shear to equibiaxial tension. The framework reproduces the characteristic U-shaped fracture locus, with maximum deviations of approximately 28% under shear and 10% under equibiaxial tension. Without recalibration, it also predicts pronounced texture sensitivity: the Cube texture increases the uniaxial fracture strain by about 47%, whereas the Brass texture suppresses the tensile peak, with fracture strains remaining between 0.2 and 0.5 for positive triaxialities. The framework therefore provides a microstructure-informed route for generating texture-sensitive fracture loci for macroscopic forming simulations. Laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) enables the fabrication of aluminum matrix particulate composites (AMPCs) with opportunities for microstructural refinement and precipitation strengthening. However, reported mechanical responses remain highly non-monotonic with respect to particle content. Strength improvements are often accompanied by limited or inconsistent gains in ductility, fatigue performance, and damage tolerance. This review adopts a constraint-first perspective and organizes the literature along a processing-linked constraint pathway. The performance of LPBF-processed AMPCs is interpreted in terms of a hierarchy of coupled physical constraints that become active at different stages. These include processing stability associated with melting behavior, interfacial mechanical and chemical compatibility under rapid thermal cycling, particle redistribution during melt-pool transport and solidification, and the transition of crack initiation control among competing defect populations. Evidence is synthesized across the full processing chain, from energy coupling at the powder bed to melt-pool dynamics, particle redistribution, and defect evolution. This framework helps explain why particle additions lead to improved mechanical performance in some cases, but not in others where processing-induced constraints become dominant. Based on this synthesis, a transferable design framework is proposed. It emphasizes stable processing conditions, interface states that sustain load transfer, control of particle clustering, and performance evaluation based on defect severity rather than average properties. Overall, this review frames LPBF-processed AMPCs as a constraint-governed system, and provides a basis for interpreting scattered results and improving cross-study comparability. This research examines the microstructure and mechanical behavior of Ti-6Al-4V/TiC components produced throughSelective Laser Melting (SLM). Four critical process variables-laser power (250–350 W), scan speed (700–1500 mm/s),layer thickness (40–60 μm), and hatch spacing (100 –150 μm) were systematically analyzed via Response SurfaceMethodology (RSM), and second-order predictive models were built to correlate these parameters with the resultingmechanical properties. Under optimal processing conditions, the fabricated specimens achieved peak values of 1195.69 MPa in tensile strength and 1284.45 MPa in flexural strength. Microstructural analysis, conducted using SEM, X-ray and EDX, revealed strong interlayer fusion, uniform distribution of alloying elements, and a low incidence of internal defects, while the material’s deformation characteristics were further evaluated through true stress–true strain curves and strainhardening behavior. https://github.com/lwz20210407/ZotWatch/issues/new?title=%5BZotWatch+feedback%5D+%E6%9A%82%E7%BC%93%E8%87%AA%E5%8A%A8%E6%8E%A8%E8%8D%90+Adaptive+peridynamic+neural+operators+with+fracture-aware+topology&body=%3C%21--+zotwatch-feedback-v2+--%3E%0A%60%60%60json%0A%7B%22doi%22%3A+%2210.1177%2F10812865261486839%22%2C+%22rating%22%3A+%22later%22%2C+%22facets%22%3A+%5B%22other_metals%22%5D%2C+%22reason%22%3A+%22%22%2C+%22applicability%22%3A+%22hold%22%7D%0A%60%60%60%0A%E5%85%AC%E5%BC%80%E5%8F%8D%E9%A6%88%EF%BC%8C%E8%AF%B7%E5%8B%BF%E5%A1%AB%E5%86%99%E7%A7%81%E4%BA%BA%E7%AC%94%E8%AE%B0%E3%80%82 Predicting fracture in complex engineering systems requires the simultaneous treatment of nonlocal constitutive behaviour, multi-physics loading and multi-scale crack propagation – a combination that no existing framework addresses in a unified, data-driven way. Existing peridynamic neural operators use a fixed horizon that either over-smooths the crack tip or sacrifices the nonlocal bulk response, and none track how a material’s connectivity changes as it fractures. We introduce the adaptive peridynamic neural operator with fracture-aware topology, which learns bond-level constitutive laws inside a damage-adaptive peridynamic operator, couples a coarse (bulk) and fine (crack-tip) operator through a multi-fidelity mixture and tracks the topology of the fracturing domain through a bond-count invariant, while remaining trainable from simulation or experimental data. Applied to biological soft tissue, ductile metals, polymers, concrete and foams, the adaptive peridynamic neural operator with fracture-aware topology achieves a mean prediction error ≈ 4 . 1 % , against 9 . 0 % for the base peridynamic neural operator and 15 . 8 % for the Fourier neural operator. Five extended physics features (anisotropic horizon, thermomechanical coupling, grain-boundary kernel, learned Paris fatigue law, electro-mechanical coupling) extend the framework to artificial intelligence chip reliability – silicon die cracking, copper pillar fatigue, underfill delamination, through-silicon via (TSV) liner cracking and low-k dielectric fracture – where the full model reaches ≈ 2 . 7 % mean prediction error ( 70 % lower than the base peridynamic neural operator), outperforms the ANSYS cohesive-zone finite element method by 3 . 5 × in accuracy while running 18 × faster and yields three quantitative design rules for bump pitch, low-k material selection and TSV keep-out zones. Published: 2026-10-27T00:00:00+00:00 Venue: Mathematics and Mechanics of Solids 研究类型: 跨金属方法参考

https://github.com/lwz20210407/ZotWatch/issues/new?title=%5BZotWatch+feedback%5D+%E6%9A%82%E7%BC%93%E8%87%AA%E5%8A%A8%E6%8E%A8%E8%8D%90+Element-level+elastoplastic+integration+for+hybrid+finite+elements+via+physics-informed+ne&body=%3C%21--+zotwatch-feedback-v2+--%3E%0A%60%60%60json%0A%7B%22doi%22%3A+%2210.1016%2Fj.cma.2026.119463%22%2C+%22rating%22%3A+%22later%22%2C+%22facets%22%3A+%5B%22plasticity_hardening%22%2C+%22calibration%22%2C+%22umat_implementation%22%5D%2C+%22reason%22%3A+%22%22%2C+%22applicability%22%3A+%22hold%22%7D%0A%60%60%60%0A%E5%85%AC%E5%BC%80%E5%8F%8D%E9%A6%88%EF%BC%8C%E8%AF%B7%E5%8B%BF%E5%A1%AB%E5%86%99%E7%A7%81%E4%BA%BA%E7%AC%94%E8%AE%B0%E3%80%82 Hybrid finite elements have proved highly accurate in plasticity problems, particularly when the assumed stress interpolation satisfies the equilibrium equations a priori. However, enforcing plastic admissibility in these formulations requires element-level constitutive updates, typically involving constrained local optimisation problems whose cost increases with the number of stress parameters and control points. This work proposes an unsupervised physics-informed neural network surrogate to accelerate the element-level return mapping in incremental elastoplastic analyses based on hybrid finite element discretisations. The network is trained by embedding the governing plasticity conditions directly during the learning process and is used to approximate the plastically corrected stress parameters from an elastic trial stress state. The strategy is tested on a plane-stress hybrid element with a five-parameter equilibrated stress field, including additional inputs that describe distorted element configurations. The results show excellent agreement with standard element-level return-mapping solutions in terms of equilibrium paths, limit loads, and stress-field reconstruction and generally reduce the number of global equilibrium iterations in the tested examples. Overall, the proposed approach achieves speed-up factors ranging from two to eight, suggesting an effective route for accelerating hybrid finite element elastoplastic analyses while retaining accuracy. https://github.com/lwz20210407/ZotWatch/issues/new?title=%5BZotWatch+feedback%5D+%E6%9A%82%E7%BC%93%E8%87%AA%E5%8A%A8%E6%8E%A8%E8%8D%90+Regulation+of+Finishing+Cooling+Temperatures+on+Microstructure+and+Comprehensive+Mechanica&body=%3C%21--+zotwatch-feedback-v2+--%3E%0A%60%60%60json%0A%7B%22doi%22%3A+%2210.1002%2Fsrin.70768%22%2C+%22rating%22%3A+%22later%22%2C+%22facets%22%3A+%5B%22temperature%22%2C+%22plasticity_hardening%22%5D%2C+%22reason%22%3A+%22%22%2C+%22applicability%22%3A+%22hold%22%7D%0A%60%60%60%0A%E5%85%AC%E5%BC%80%E5%8F%8D%E9%A6%88%EF%BC%8C%E8%AF%B7%E5%8B%BF%E5%A1%AB%E5%86%99%E7%A7%81%E4%BA%BA%E7%AC%94%E8%AE%B0%E3%80%82 A Gleeble‐3500 thermo‐mechanical simulator was employed for this study. The effects of finishing cooling temperatures (450/500/550/600 °C) on the microstructural evolution and mechanical properties of a novel V–Ti–N microalloyed high‐heat‐input weathering steel were investigated. The results show that with the increase of finishing cooling temperature, the proportion of polygonal ferrite (PF) increases, the fraction of granular bainitic ferrite decreases markedly, while the proportion of acicular ferrite increases slightly. The area fraction and size of M/A constituents increase, and the dislocation density reduces. Higher finishing cooling temperature causes microstructure coarsening. It diminishes dislocation substructures and decreases the strength and low‐temperature impact toughness. However, the increase in PF and coarsening of M/A constituents enhance the strain‐hardening capacity, slowing down the reduction in tensile strength, lowering the yield ratio, and improving the elongation after fracture. Based on the comprehensive performance evaluation, controlling the finishing cooling temperature at 500–550 °C achieves a good balance between strength, ductility, toughness, and yield ratio, resulting in excellent comprehensive mechanical properties. This study provides important theoretical and practical references for the preparation of high‐performance microalloyed high‐heat‐input steel by thermo‐mechanical control process. item.title: Influence of defects on mechanical properties of Ti–6Al–4V components produced by selective laser melting and electron beam melting
item.description: 经典文献补漏 库内相似论文：Comparison of the microstructures and mechanical properties of ti–6Al–4V fabricated by selective laser melting and electron beam melting（相似度 0.870） 被相关论文引用：Fracture of laser powder bed fusion additively manufactured Ti–6Al–4V under multiaxial loading: Calibration and comparison of fracture models [https://doi.org/10.1016/j.msea.2019.05.097] 与《Heterogeneous random medium plasticity and fracture model of additively-manufactured Ti-6Al-4V》共享 2 篇参考文献；归一化重合度 0.047 共享参考文献示例：https://openalex.org/W2014521333, https://openalex.org/W2014734472 增材 TC4 缺陷与力学响应: 可作为缺陷形貌与成形方向如何改变塑性流动和断裂行为的机制线索（规则推断，非已验证迁移） 迁移前检查: 核对是否给出应力应变或断裂数据（而非只有组织照片）、制备参数与热处理状态、是否与你的试样同一工艺窗口 仅题名片段: Influence of defects on mechanical properties … 标题/摘要不能确认全部实验条件与方法适用性，未陈述内容保持未知 公开阅读反馈 Abstract Laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) imposes steep thermal gradients, resulting in distortion and the formation of significant residual stresses, which often precipitate in-situ cracking at support interfaces and sharp geometric features. To isolate their influence on structural integrity, we combined fracture mechanics testing with residual stress evaluation on as-built compact tension specimens printed in two orthogonal orientations. The experimentally measured apparent stress-intensity factor was deconvolved into mechanical and residual-stress components, yielding a residual-stress-free fracture toughness (\(\:{K}_{ICeff}\)). Apparent fracture toughness ranged from 25–35 MPa.m 1/2 , whereas \(\:{K}_{ICeff}\) increased to 45–52 MPa.m 1/2 . Residual stresses, therefore, depress the material’s residual-stress-free resistance by up to ~ 50% and accentuate orientation-dependent anisotropy. The framework presented offers a route for quantifying process-induced toughness degradation in LPBF alloys.
